paragraphs.text: Son of Nabopolassar who founded the Babylonian monarchy.
paragraphs.anchor: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

paragraphs.text: sc., After that he had beaten the king of Egypt’s forces at Charchemish. {Jer 46:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Came up

paragraphs.text: Defectione tam turpi quam exitiosa. The king of Egypt by fair promises prevailed with him to rebel against Nebuchadnezzar, as also by threats, that otherwise he would restore Jehoahaz now prisoner in Egypt; which yet Jeremiah assured him should never be. {Jer 22:11-12}
paragraphs.anchor: Then he turned and rebelled against him.

paragraphs.text: Latrunculos the Vulgate renders it. Soldiers that fight in an evil cause are no better than robbers and spoilers. Josephus saith that Nebuchadnezzar, bringing from that siege of Tyre {Eze 26:7} some part of his army, entered therewith Jerusalem, slew Jehoiakim, and cast him out unburied, according to Jer 22:18-19, carrying away three thousand and three and twenty Jews. {Jer 52:28} And here began the seventy years’ captivity: now was Daniel and his companions brought to Babylon, {Dan 1:3-7} according to Isa 39:7.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord sent against him bands.

paragraphs.text: Heb., At the mouth, i.e., Ex praestituto. God’s holy hand is in all the miseries that befall his people. {Amo 3:6}
paragraphs.anchor: Surely at the commandment of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Or, For the like sins to those which Manasseh had done, as Tremellius rendereth it, Traiectio, as in Gen 5:29 Jdg 18:31.
paragraphs.anchor: For the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did.

paragraphs.text: Of this crying sin Jehoahaz also and Jehoiakim were deeply guilty. {Jer 22:17 Eze 19:1-14}
paragraphs.anchor: And also for the innocent blood.

paragraphs.text: See 1Ki 15:23.
paragraphs.anchor: Now the rest of the acts.

paragraphs.text: Respectu habito ad communem naturae legem; Jehoiakim died, being slain in Jerusalem, and as "an ass cast forth beyond the gates"; {Jer 22:18-19} or else, going captive to Babylon, he died by the way, ingloria vita recessit, without burial or mourning. {2Ch 36:6} He is also cut out of the roll of the kings of Judah. {Mat 1:11}
paragraphs.anchor: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers.

paragraphs.text: About this time died Nabopolassar the father of Nebuchadnezzar: whereupon he, committing the care of his captives to his friends in the army, hastened to Babylon, where, taking upon him the empire, he distributed the captives by colonies into fit places in the country of Babylon, as saith Berosus. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: For the king of Babylon had taken.

paragraphs.text: {a} Rer. Chald., lib. xxx.

sc., When he began to reign alone. See 2Ch 36:9. Mutavit Iudaea dominos, non miserias. This king is also called Jechonias, {Mat 1:11} and Coniah - that is, prepared, sc., for destruction; {Jer 22:24} the name of God - whom he had forsaken - being defalked. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Jehoiakin was eighteen years old

paragraphs.text: {a} [Withdrawn; i.e., Je (Jehovah) left out of his name Jeconiah.]
See 1Ki 11:16.
paragraphs.anchor: And he did.

paragraphs.text: About the spring. {2Ch 36:10} Much about the same time was Cyrus born for a scourge to Babylon, {a} but for a relief to God’s poor prisoners of hope there; according as Isaiah had foretold, {Isa 47:1-2; Isa 13:16} and the psalmist. {Psa 137:8-9} See Isa 44:28; Isa 45:1-4.
paragraphs.anchor: At that time.

paragraphs.text: {a} Cic. de Divin. ex Dionys.

Till their king came himself in person, and entered the city, as Sulpitius hath it: but whereas he addeth, that at this time, urbem murosque ac templum solo stravit, this is utterly false; for Jehoiachin, by yielding up the city, as Jeremiah had advised him, preserved it; wherein he did the part of a good king, saith Josephus.
paragraphs.anchor: And his servants did besiege it.

paragraphs.text: Suscepit eum; gratiose scilicet; he gave him quarter for his life, and in the end, for a reward of his obedience and piety towards his country, he was much advanced by Evilmerodaeh, Nebuchadnezsar’s successor. {2Ki 25:27}
paragraphs.anchor: And the king of Babylon took him.

paragraphs.text: That is, All that he met with, or thought meet. See 2Ki 25:13-15.
paragraphs.anchor: All the treasures.

paragraphs.text: Yet not all neither. See Ezr 1:7.
paragraphs.anchor: And cut in pieces all.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The greater and better part of the people: among the rest, Mordecai the Benjamite the son of Jair, {Est 2:5-6} and Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, {Eze 1:2-3} who therefore calls it his "captivity" or deportation. {Eze 40:1}
paragraphs.anchor: And he carried away all Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The like craft useth the devil, when he endeavoureth to take out of the way such as are zealous and active, valiant for God’s truth, and violent for his kingdom. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And all the craftsmen and smiths.

paragraphs.text: {a} A Lapide.
Where it fared better with them than with those that were left behind. {Jer 24:4-5, &c.} To these the prophet Jeremiah wrote a letter, if Apocryphal Baruch may be believed. {/APC Bar 6:1}
paragraphs.anchor: These carried he into captivity into Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Eighteen thousand in all; this was the second captivity.
paragraphs.anchor: Craftsmen, &c.

paragraphs.text: His name signifieth God’s gift, the same as Nathanael, Theodore, Diodate. Good Josiah gave all his children good names but they proved all stark naught.
paragraphs.anchor: And the king of Babylon had made Mattaniah.

paragraphs.text: But had small joy of his kingdom; so had King John of England.
paragraphs.anchor: And he reigned eleven years.

paragraphs.text: Breaking covenant both with God, {Jer 34:17} and with men. {Eze 17:18-19}
paragraphs.anchor: And he did that which was evil.

paragraphs.text: Who hardened Zedekiah’s heart, that he "humbled not himself before Jeremiah," &c. {2Ch 36:12}
paragraphs.anchor: For through the anger of the Lord.
